chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman who enters Mecca performing Tamattu' Hajj and menstruates before she exits the state of Ihram for Umrah, asking when her Tamattu' ends. He said: 'Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The disappearance of the sun on the day of Tarwiyah.' And Musa (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The morning prayer on the day of Tarwiyah.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, most of your followers enter on the day of Tarwiyah, perform Tawaf and Sa'i, then enter Ihram for Hajj.' He said: 'The disappearance of the sun.' I mentioned to him the narration of Ajlan Abu Salih, so he said: 'No, when the sun sets, the Tamattu' is gone.' I said: 'Is she still in her Ihram, or does she renew her Ihram for Hajj?' He said: 'No, she remains in her Ihram.' I said: 'Is there a sacrifice upon her?' He said: 'No, unless she wishes to volunteer.' Then he said: 'As for us, if we see the crescent of Dhul-Hijjah before we enter Ihram, the Tamattu' is lost to us.'

And the fundamental principle regarding the loss of Tamattu' is what we have previously mentioned, namely: Whenever it becomes predominant in a person's opinion that if he delays exiting the time in which he is currently situated, he will miss the Standing (at Arafat), then he has no Tamattu'. And whenever he knows or it becomes predominant in his opinion that he will join the people at Arafat after fulfilling what is upon him from the rituals of Umrah, then his Umrah is complete. And we have explained that with a sufficient explanation. And this also confirms here specifically in the matter of the menstruating woman, what has been narrated.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.اَلتَّرْوِيَةُ: The day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلْإِحْرَامُ: Ihram (the state of consecration for pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: When does the Umrah portion of Tamattu' Hajj end for a menstruating woman, and does she need to renew her Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of the menstruating woman in Tamattu' Hajj, resolving the dispute between Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Imam Musa al-Kazim regarding the precise cutoff time for the Umrah portion. It establishes the practical ruling that she retains her Ihram status without penalty, while linking this specific case to the broader principle that Tamattu' is forfeited if there is a strong probability of missing the Arafat stand. The text also notes the Imams' own practice of considering the Tamattu' void if the new moon of Dhu al-Hijjah appears before their own Ihram, highlighting the importance of timing in ritual validity.
